title: Fix rule binding precedence when edge scope is elided
body:
Without build-local bindings, a file-level `command` can shadow the rule's command; adding an unused binding changes which command runs. Track whether an edge has its own environment so lookup follows the documented build > rule > file order while retaining lazy environment allocation.

Dyndep `restat` updates now create a local environment when necessary, so they override the rule without leaking to other edges. Regressions cover empty overrides, late expansion, include/subninja scopes and dyndep isolation.

Fixes #1516.

Validated with MSVC x64 Debug and Release builds, installed CLI builds and incremental rebuilds. Both native suites pass 442/443 tests; the same symlink-creation test fails on unchanged master. Python checks pass 39 tests with 28 skips and 9 Windows failures also reproduced on master. The existing manifest benchmark stayed within about 1% in this local comparison, and `sizeof(Edge)` remained 160 bytes.

title: Fix negative node_id OOB in deps log parser
body:
## Summary
Fixes an out-of-bounds read (SIGSEGV) in the `.ninja_deps` log parser, an unpatched sibling of the fix in PR #2825.

## Details
PR #2825 fixed `DepsLog::Load()` accepting a deps record whose `out_id` was past the path table, but the validation it added is asymmetric:

- `out_id` is checked with `out_id < 0 || out_id >= (int)nodes_.size()`,
- while each dependency entry is only checked with `node_id >= (int)nodes_.size() || !nodes_[node_id]` — the `node_id < 0` check is missing.

A deps record containing a negative `node_id` (e.g. -1) therefore passes validation: `nodes_[-1]` performs an out-of-bounds read on the `vector<Node*>` backing store (converted to a huge `size_t` index), and the garbage pointer is stored into the in-memory `Deps` entry. It is later dereferenced, e.g. by `ninja -t deps` (`deps->nodes[i]->path()`) or by `ImplicitDepLoader::LoadDepsFromLog` (`nodes[i]->AddOutEdge(edge)`), crashing ninja (SIGSEGV).

Additionally, a deps record shorter than 12 bytes (`out_id` + 8-byte mtime) makes `deps_count = size/4 - 3` negative, and the negative value is passed to `new Node*[node_count]` in the `Deps` constructor, aborting the process via `std::bad_array_new_length`/`std::bad_alloc`.

Both are reachable with a crafted `.ninja_deps` file, which ninja loads automatically at startup on every build.

The patch rejects deps records smaller than 12 bytes and rejects negative node ids, treating both the same as a truncated file (truncate + recover), exactly like the `out_id` case.

## Testing
- PoC verified: crafted `.ninja_deps` with `node_id = -1` crashes ninja (SIGSEGV) before the fix; after the fix the record is rejected and ninja recovers.
- Short-record PoC (10 bytes) aborts before the fix; rejected cleanly after.

**AI tool use disclosure:** AI was used in part for code audit and patch drafting.

title: reject negative dependency ids when loading deps log
body:
Repro: load a `.ninja_deps` whose deps record carries a negative dependency id (e.g. `0xffffffff`) under a valid out_id. Built with `-fsanitize=address`, `DepsLog::Load` reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ at deps_log.cc:229.

Cause: the out_id guard added in 5e4ac66 rejects `out_id < 0`, but the per-dependency loop only tests `node_id >= nodes_.size()`. A negative id slips past that comparison, so `nodes_[node_id]` indexes the vector before its start, and a non-null garbage read would be stored straight into `deps->nodes` and later dereferenced during the build.

Fix: apply the same `node_id < 0` check the out_id path already uses. Added a regression test next to RecompactBogusOutId that crafts a record with dep id -1 and expects the loader to recover instead of indexing out of bounds.

title: create jobserver pool fifo with owner-only permissions
body: the fifo that PosixJobserverPool::InitWithFifo creates in $TMPDIR (/tmp by default) is made with mode 0666, so with the usual 022 umask every local user can read it, and with a looser umask write to it too. anyone who can open it can drain job slots out of the pool, leaving the build and its sub-makes on the implicit slot, or push extra slots in past -j. GNU make creates its jobserver fifo with 0600, so InitWithFifo now does the same, and so does create_fifo in misc/jobserver_pool.py which had the same default. JobserverPoolTest.FifoIsOwnerOnly clears the umask and stats the fifo: it fails on master with the group/other rw bits set and passes with this change.

title: Forward SIGTERM to console pool subprocesses
body:
Addresses the SIGTERM-to-ninja case in #2116.

A `pool = console` job runs in ninja's process group, so `SubprocessSet::Clear()` skips it on the assumption that it received the same signal ninja did. That's true for Ctrl-C (SIGINT) and terminal hangup (SIGHUP), but SIGTERM from a service manager or a plain `kill <pid>` reaches only ninja. Ninja then marks the build as interrupted and blocks in `Clear()` until the console job exits on its own.

This forwards SIGTERM to console subprocesses by PID. The child is in ninja's process group, so it can't be signalled as a group the way other jobs are. SIGINT and SIGHUP are still left to the terminal so the child doesn't get them twice. Directly sent SIGINT and termination of descendants of a console shell are outside this fix. If SIGTERM was sent to the whole process group, the console job now gets a second SIGTERM, which doesn't matter for the default disposition.

With the `build.ninja` from the issue (`sleep 100` in the console pool), `kill -TERM <ninja>` used to leave ninja waiting ~99s before it exited. With this change it exits immediately.

Added `SubprocessTest.InterruptParentWithSigTermConsole`, which fails without the fix (`Clear()` takes 30s) and passes with it. `ninja_test` passes on Linux (433 tests).

title: Continue to ignore hangups in subprocesses if SIGHUP is ignored
body:
Currently, if SIGHUP is ignored when ninja is spawned, ninja will continue to ignore it.

However, each subprocess spawned has it's handler set manually, catching the signal as a result, however, with a delay, and causes ninja to close anyway, with similar behavior as if ninja's handler was reset, but with a different exit code. In this case, ninja happens to mask the true cause of the exit, while child processes have the exit code associated with hangups.

Let SIGHUP be first in the list to configure a subprocess according to the standard numerical order,
and first check whether SIGHUP is ignored
before setting the signal for that process to a custom handler.

title: Fix depfile loading after restat processing
body:
Thanks for the guys finding this issue in the Ninja fork used to build Bun. The relevant changes can be found here: - [commit](https://github.com/ninja-build/ninja/commit/5ecd88315d1147a0d84cb79002043638f415d239) - [readme.md](https://github.com/oven-sh/ninja/tree/bun/bun). ### Issue #2680 changed how depfiles are loaded to prevent stale depfiles from being loaded when the corresponding edge is dirty. However, an edge with a restatted input is only potentially dirty at that point. Its final dirty state can only be determined after the restat input has been processed. If the restat input's timestamp has not changed, the edge may turn out to be clean. In that case, the depfile still needs to be loaded, but the current logic has already skipped loading it based on the edge's initial dirty state. This can therefore result in a required depfile not being loaded when an edge becomes clean after restat processing. This issue was introduced by #2680, as depfiles were previously loaded unconditionally. ### Proposed Solution Once a restatted input has been processed, the output edge of that input needs to be reevaluated to determine whether they are dirty or clean. If an edge changes from dirty to clean as a result of restat processing, its depfile must be loaded at that point. The inputs loaded from the depfile may be source files or generated nodes and may introduce arbitrary dependency graphs. These dependencies therefore need to be added to the already explored graph. A similar issue with `ninja -t explain`, where the initial explanation was not updated after restat processing, is resolved as well. ### Example
Build file ```ninja rule true command = cmp -s $in $out || cp $in $out restat = 1 rule cp command = cp $src $out && printf '%s: %s\n' "$out" "$dep_input" > $depfile depfile = $out.d build B: true A build C: cp B src = B dep_input = X ```
### Current master branch Initially build is clean. Ninja needs to be called twice to build all nodes, as the depfile is not loaded. ```console $ touch A X && ninja C -d explain -v ninja explain: recorded mtime of B older than most recent input A (1790522029645083862 vs 1790522055713064511) [1/2] cmp -s A B || cp A B $ ninja C -d explain -v ninja explain: output C older than most recent input X (1790522029651084089 vs 1790522055713064511) [1/1] cp B C && printf '%s: %s\n' "C" "X" > C.d $ ninja C -d explain -v ninja: no work to do. ``` ### Proposed Solution Initially build is clean. Ninja needs to be called once to build all nodes. ```console $ touch A X && ninja C -d explain -v ninja explain: recorded mtime of B older than most recent input A (1790522055718064698 vs 1790522256617467699) [1/2] cmp -s A B || cp A B ninja explain: output C older than most recent input X (1790522077112865272 vs 1790522256617467699) [2/2] cp B C && printf '%s: %s\n' "C" "X" > C.d $ ninja C -d explain -v ninja: no work to do. ``` Ninja prior PR #2680 behaves like this.

title: diagnostics: include previous rule context in multiple rules generate…
body:
Closes #2659

### Problem
When multiple rules generate the same output file, Ninja outputs:

ninja: error: multiple rules generate

On large build graphs, this error doesn't tell the user which earlier rule or input introduced the output first, making it difficult to trace conflicting build statements.

### Solution
Added `Edge::FormatDuplicateRuleError()` to inspect the existing edge producing the node and include rule context:
- For edges with a single input:
  `multiple rules generate foo (previously defined by rule 'compile' with input 'a.c')`
- For edges with multiple inputs:
  `multiple rules generate foo (previously defined by rule 'link' with inputs ['a.o', 'b.o'])`
- For rules with no inputs:
  `multiple rules generate foo (previously defined by rule 'touch')`

Wired this through both static parsing (`State::AddOut`) and dynamic dependencies (`DyndepLoader::UpdateEdge`), and updated/added test coverage in `manifest_parser_test.cc`, `graph_test.cc`, and `build_test.cc`.

title: Invalidate Iterator in RecomputeNodeDirty
body:
https://github.com/ninja-build/ninja/blob/c8b233e8053c03d2fd57389035b47d36e98e69a8/src/graph.cc#L364-L371

Calling `RecomputeNodeDirty` from the range-based loop over `edge->inputs_` may invalidate the loop iterator.

This can happen when `RecomputeNodeDirty` loads new dynamic dependencies and adds inputs to the node's edge. Since edge->inputs_ is a std::vector, adding elements may trigger a reallocation and invalidate the iterators used by the range-based loop, resulting in undefined behavior.

This PR switches to index-based iteration to avoid using iterators that may be invalidated while processing the inputs.

title: ninja_syntax: escape paths in Writer.default
body:
`Writer.build` already runs `escape_path` on outputs and inputs, but `Writer.default` joined paths raw. A single default target with a space was therefore emitted as two defaults.

Use `escape_path` for each path, matching the rest of the Writer API. Suggested on #990 (and in closed #1067).

The added tests fail on the unpatched helper (`default foo bar` with a space) and pass with this change.

```
python3 -m pytest misc/ninja_syntax_test.py -q
# 28 passed
```

title: ninja_syntax: escape dollar signs in paths
body:
`escape_path` escaped spaces and colons, but left a bare `$` in place. Ninja treats `$` as the escape/variable character, so a generated edge with `foo$bar` is parsed as `foo` plus variable `bar`.

Escape `$` first. `foo$bar` becomes `foo$$bar`. Dollar-space still becomes `$$$ ` (literal `$` plus an escaped space), same as before.

A path that already starts with a ninja variable (`$root/...`, `$builddir/...`) is generator syntax from `configure.py`, not a filename that starts with `$`. Those prefixes stay unescaped so bootstrap still finds `configure.py`.

The added tests fail on the unpatched helper (`foo$bar` is unchanged) and pass with this change.

title: Add a pcons build
body:
Port the CMake build of ninja to pcons (https://pcons.org). To try it:
```
uvx pcons
```

There are lots of options; I tried to replicate the cmake build for the most part. NINJA_CLANG_TIDY uses pcons's built-in clang-tidy support, so this needs pcons 0.29.0 or later. Closes #2829 .

title: Enable tweaking the scheduling order for first-time builds via explicit targets
body:
This is a stab at https://github.com/ninja-build/ninja/issues/232, allowing to tweak the scheduling order via e.g. `ninja <slow output> all`, for first-time builds without previous build times yet, such as fresh CI builds in ephemeral containers.

Implemented by overriding the weight of target-producing edges iff.
* multiple targets have been specified, and
* there is no previous build time for that edge yet.

This target-order-specific weight is stored in the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit weight, starting with 1<<32 for the last target's edge, 2<<32 for the 2nd-last target's, 3<<32 for the 3rd-last etc. It should thus always dominate normal weights (e.g., elapsed milliseconds for the previous build).

(Something similar to this was implemented in #2019, but not in accepted #2177. With #2686 having landed, I think this is the last remaining interesting piece from #2019.)
